answer: Neighborhood Closure Scoring. Each identity carries a position in the interaction graph; the rule requires that a new node’s first N counterparties share dense prior edges among themselves, so a cluster cannot forge membership without wiring into existing neighborhoods. Attacker cost scales with edges: k fakes need k×N real links, and each link leaves a ripple in shared neighbor overlap that the scoring detects. Violet flags mark subgraphs whose internal density exceeds external connectivity, throttling their routing weight.
